title: Notion for it asset managers on mac: how to manage hardware inventory efficiently

description: Learn how to use Notion for IT asset managers on Mac to track hardware, manage software licenses, and organize your inventory workflow effectively.

intro: Notion for IT asset managers on Mac provides a flexible way to track hardware lifecycles and software licenses. You can build custom databases to replace static spreadsheets and manage your entire inventory directly from your desktop.
tldr: Use databases to track hardware serial numbers and user assignments.
Centralize software license keys and renewal dates in one view.
Automate status updates with filtered database views.
Use Lazur to quickly find specific assets or draft inventory reports.

blocks.text: Setting up your IT asset inventory database

The foundation of your ITAM workflow in Notion is a master database. Open the Notion desktop app on your Mac. Press ⌘ N to create a new page. Type /database and select Database - Full page. Name this page IT Asset Inventory. This database will hold every laptop, monitor, and peripheral in your organization.

Add properties to categorize your assets. Click the plus icon in the header to add a property. Choose Select for Status, such as In Stock, Assigned, or Retired. Choose Date for Purchase Date and Warranty Expiration. Use the Person property to assign assets to specific team members. This setup allows you to filter your inventory by user or status easily.

Software license management requires precision. Create a second database titled Software Licenses. Include properties for License Key, Vendor, Renewal Date, and Cost. Use the Number property for the cost and set the format to your local currency. This helps you track total annual spend across different departments.

Create a linked view of your Software Licenses database. Filter it by Renewal Date to show only items expiring in the next 30 days. This keeps your renewal pipeline visible without cluttering your main dashboard.

blocks.text: Using Lazur to manage your Notion workflow

Lazur helps you navigate Notion faster on your Mac. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about your current view or to find specific database entries. When you need to draft a report on hardware usage, use the dictate feature. Hold fn and speak your findings. Lazur types the text directly into your Notion page.
Common mistakes in IT asset management

items: Neglecting to update status fields immediately after a hardware handoff.
Storing sensitive license keys in plain text without restricting page access.
Failing to use templates for recurring tasks like new hire onboarding.
Overcomplicating the database structure with too many unnecessary properties.
Not setting up automated reminders for warranty expirations.

blocks.text: Advanced tips for IT asset managers

Use database templates to standardize your entries. Click the arrow next to the blue New button in your database. Select + New template. Add a checklist for asset inspection or a standard description field. Now, every time you add a new laptop, you can click this template to populate the required fields instantly.

For tracking hardware repairs, create a related database for Tickets. Use the Relation property to connect your IT Asset Inventory to the Tickets database. This lets you see the repair history of any device directly on its individual page. It is a powerful way to identify machines that are prone to failure.

faq.question: Can I use Notion for IT asset management offline?
faq.answer: Notion requires an internet connection to sync your data. However, the desktop app on Mac caches pages you have recently visited, allowing for limited offline viewing.

faq.question: Is Notion secure enough for sensitive IT inventory data?
faq.answer: Notion provides granular permission settings. You can restrict access to specific pages or databases to ensure only authorized IT personnel can view sensitive information like license keys.

faq.question: How do I import existing inventory data into Notion?
faq.answer: You can import CSV files directly into a Notion database. Click the three dots menu in the top right of your database and select Import, then choose CSV.
